text: Dolores María Fonzi (born 19 July 1978) is an Argentine television, theatre, and film actress. Several of her films have received critical acclaim, including Burnt Money (2000), Waiting for the Messiah (2000), Bottom of the Sea (2003), The Aura (2005), and Paulina (2015). In 2023, she made her directorial debut with the comedy-drama Blondi.[1] Her second film, the legal drama Belén, is competing for the Golden Shell at the 73rd San Sebastian International Film Festival.[2] She was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and after her parents' separation, her mother, María del Rosario Cárrega, returned with her children to Adrogué, where Dolores and her brothers Tomás and Diego grew up. She studied acting at the school of Carlos Gandolfo; her brother Tomás Fonzi is also an actor in Argentina.[3][4] In 1996, at seventeen years old, she made her first television appearance in the series La nena. In 1998, Cris Morena chose her to play Clara Vázquez in Verano del '98, alongside her brother, who played Benjamín Vázquez. Thanks to the series' success and her portrayal as a villain, she gained significant popularity and success. At the end of 1999, she left Verano del '98 to join Marcelo Piñeyro's film Burnt Money, marking her film debut in a role as a sex worker.[5] She also appeared in Waiting for the Messiah. In 2001, she gained recognition by joining the cast of El sodero de mi vida on Canal 13, where she played a girl with a slight mental retardation. She experimented with Luis Ortega on the tape Caja negra, where she acted and participated in the integral creation. She later appeared in films such as Private Lives, Bottom of the Sea, The Aura, La mujer rota, Salamandra, El club de la muerte, and El campo, for which she was nominated for the Silver Condor Awards for Best Actress. In 2003, she starred in the unitary series Disputas and in the adaptation of John Ford's play Lástima que sea una puta. The following year, she starred with Mariano Martínez in the terror unit Sangre fría on Telefe. From 2006 to 2014, she starred and produced the miniseries Soy tu fan, which was adapted by Canana Films in Mexico in 2010. She also starred in the series El tiempo no para on Canal 9. From 2005 to 2008, she participated in three chapters of Mujeres asesinas. Her return to television was in 2012 with her role in Graduados, a new Underground production for Telefe. She also participated in the TV Pública series En terapia with actors Norma Aleandro, Diego Peretti, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Ailín Salas, Julieta Cardinali, and Germán Palacios. She resumed her theater career as the protagonist of the play Isósceles. That year, she also filmed El Crítico by Hernán Guerschuny, a co-production between HC Films and Lagarto Cine, where she had the lead alongside Rafael Spregelburd. On television, she appeared as a guest actress in two episodes of the series Aliados. In 2015, she starred in the film Paulina, a remake of the 1960 film starring Mirtha Legrand. The film achieved strong box office performance and favorable reviews, being praised at the Cannes Festival. For her performance, she was awarded the Havana Star Prize for Best Actress at the 17th Havana Film Festival New York.[6] She also acted in the film Truman starring Ricardo Darín. In 2016, she joined the cast of the series La Leona, playing Eugenia Leone. From 2008 to 2014, she was in a relationship with actor Gael García Bernal,[7] whom she met on the set of the 2001 film Private Lives.[8] They had two children, born in 2009 and 2011.[7] Afterward, she entered a relationship with filmmaker Santiago Mitre, whom she met during the filming of Paulina in 2014.[9]
